director.chapterArc: A tense survival sequence where Callie discovers her power's mechanics (leaning vs. pushing) and realizes she is 'lit' by a second force that isolates her from physical contact with food or touch.
director.restraintNote: The scene requires extreme vocal restraint during the discovery of the Edge mechanism; avoid making it sound like a magic spell reveal, treat it as a cold, mechanical realization. The emotional climax (mother's hand) must be delivered without melodrama, focusing on the physical impossibility rather than sadness.

cues.delivery: Establish the visual of the broken span with a grounded, observational tone. Convey the danger through physical description rather than fear.
cues.from: The causeway simply stopped. The concrete deck ended in a broken lip with rusted rod hanging out of it like hair. Past the lip there were eight lengths of rail iron laid side by side, bolted down at either end, running out across the dark to where Katori's lamp could just find the far lip forty feet away. There were gaps between the rails a hand wide. Through the gaps there was nothing at all. The lamp went down into them and did not come back.
cues.through: Duchess stood at the edge of it with her forefeet planted and her head up and her nostrils going. She was not screaming now. She was past that. She was simply not going to move, the way a post is not going to move, and Otto stood at her head stroking her neck with his good hand and saying, "It's all right, it's all right, it's all right," like a man bailing a boat with a cup.
cues.reason: Scene setting for the causeway crossing.

cues.delivery: Pell's dialogue should be dry and factual. The rhythm is steady; he is stating logistics, not panicking.
cues.from: "The iron's fine," he said. "The iron'll take the wagon. It's taken wagons for eleven years, she says, and I believe her." He came back. "The iron's not the trouble. The trouble is that a horse puts her foot down on that and it goes into a hole, and a horse with her foot in a hole will break her own leg getting it out, and then I've no horse at all. She knows that. She knew it before any of us were born." He looked at the gaps. "She's right. That's the worst of it."
cues.through: "Then use the one." Pell was already at the net, with his fingers working the knots. "And I'll want your coat for her eyes, because mine stinks of her already and she's had enough of it."
cues.reason: Establishing the logistical problem with the horse.

cues.delivery: Action beats must be precise and mechanical. The hook's movement is described as a physical extension of her body.
cues.from: It came over the west lip and she tipped it with the old curve, carefully, the way she had learned in the last hour, keeping the grey sweep up and out over its back. It went down. She turned for the second, fast, because the second was already at the lip on the east side, and the whole four feet of grey came round with her.
cues.through: Callie had not heard her come. Katori had come back down the causeway with the lamp, quietly, to see what the second sound was. She had stopped six paces off, where she always stopped. And the new length of the hook had reached six paces, and it had gone past her nose, and she had not moved at all.
cues.reason: Combat sequence requiring clarity on the physics.

cues.delivery: Katori's voice is flat and authoritative. She is giving a command that requires immediate compliance; no emotional spikes.
cues.from: "You're going to have to, before you take somebody's leg off." Katori did not raise her voice. "In about five minutes, Otto and Pell are going to lead a blind horse across forty feet of iron. Then the wagon goes over, with your mother on it. Then you go over, last, on your own. And every foot of that you'll be carrying a thing that goes through ash-wood like water, in the dark, with people in front of you. So it's going down. Now. And I'm going to help you."

cues.delivery: The internal monologue regarding the 'well' must be rhythmic and analytical. Callie is tracing a physical sensation backward.
cues.from: "No. Think. Not where it is. Where's it coming from?"
cues.through: The grey part was cold. The old curve was colder. The socket, where the bolt went through, was colder still. And the cold did not stop at the socket. It came down the conduit into her hand, and up her wrist, and into her arm. That was the cold that had got as far as her shoulders now. It went up into her shoulder, and then it went down.
cues.reason: Callie's realization of the Edge mechanism.

cues.delivery: The revelation 'She was leaning' should be delivered with a slight pause for impact. It is a factual correction of her understanding.
The physical sensation of the Edge leaving must be conveyed through pacing and breath. The hook becoming heavy is a tactile shift.
cues.from: She did it with her body first, because that was where it lived. Her hips came up and her back foot came off the brace and her weight settled back over her own heels, the way it did at the end of every sack on every rail she had ever swung one from. And somewhere down in the dark, over the top of the well, she came up off it.
cues.through: Callie sat down on the road. She did not decide to. Her legs decided, and she let them. She sat in the middle of the causeway with the hook across her knees, and she put one cold hand on the steel and felt nothing coming up out of it at all, and she did not know what she felt about that. She had not asked for it. She had not wanted it. It had been hers for two hours, the way her own tongue was hers, and now it was gone, and it felt like putting her hand in a pocket and finding a hole where something used to be.
cues.reason: Transition from power to normal state.

cues.delivery: Callie's realization that the second force is 'leaning on her' must be delivered with a quiet shock. It changes the nature of her burden.
cues.from: "I'm not leaning on that one." She could feel it very clearly now that the Edge was gone. Its weight was all around her, closed over her from boots to crown, and she could feel how different it was. "I'm not leaning on it at all. It's leaning on me."
cues.through: "Then that's tomorrow's problem," she said. "Tonight's problem has a blind horse in it."

cues.delivery: The crossing of the span is tense but quiet. The focus is on the physical danger and Callie's isolation.
cues.from: They got Duchess across with Otto's coat buttoned round her head and Pell walking backward in front of her on the boards. He talked to her the whole way, as he always did, one slow word to each step. Otto walked beside her shoulder with his good hand on her neck. She put each foot down as if the whole world might be a hole. Twice she stopped altogether in the middle of the span, with forty feet of dark under her and nobody on either side of her, and twice Pell waited until she went on, and did not hurry her, and did not stop talking.
cues.through: "Mm," said Katori, and took the hand away.

cues.delivery: The medical scene is clinical. Callie's mother speaks with authority and precision; the tone is matter-of-fact despite the injury.
cues.from: They got Otto's arm open in the lamplight at about midnight.
cues.through: Ines did it again. Her hands, which could put an arrow into a hound at ninety paces in bad light, were not quite steady, and Callie's mother saw it, and did not say anything about it. She just held the lamp a little closer.
cues.reason: Establishing the gravity of Otto's wound.

cues.delivery: The conversation about 'The Warren' provides a moment of human connection. The tone is conversational but underlined by the tension.
cues.from: "Tell me something, Otto," she said. "Anything. Where were you born?"
cues.through: Behind her, her mother was saying, "Twenty-two. That's twenty-two. You've got a good arm, Otto, it's going to be an ugly arm, but it's going to be an arm," and Otto was laughing and crying at the same time and trying to do neither.
cues.reason: Character interaction to ground the scene.

cues.delivery: Callie's attempt to eat must be delivered with a sense of physical impossibility. The narrator should convey the 'barrier' without over-explaining.
cues.from: He came to the doorway with a tin cup and a heel of bread and a strip of the dried meat they had been saving since the Warren. He stood them on the sill beside her and did not say anything, which was his way of saying something. Callie realized, looking at the bread, that she had not stopped being hungry since the ninth husk on the causeway. The hunger had got so big and so constant that she'd stopped noticing it was hunger. It had turned into the general shape of the world.
cues.through: She tried again, slower, as if it were a matter of care. The bread stopped where it had stopped before. She could not put it any closer. The thing closed over her hand met the thing closed over her face. They touched each other, and neither of them would give.

cues.delivery: Katori's diagnosis is delivered with a flat, factual tone. The 'three days' limit is stated as data, not fear.
cues.from: "You're not fine. You've been lit for five hours, and it's eating you, and you can't eat." He said it like a distance. "Katori."
cues.through: "No," Katori agreed. "I don't. I'm saying it anyway, because it's true that you found the first one, and I'd rather you heard that from me than worked it out in the dark on your own." She stood. "Sit in your door. I'll sit up with you."
cues.reason: Establishing the stakes of Callie's condition.

cues.delivery: The final interaction with her mother is intimate and quiet. The focus is on the physical impossibility of touch.
cues.from: Near two in the morning her mother called her.
cues.through: Out in the dark, on the gravel, another one was coming.

pauses.after: At night, from the tailgate of a wagon, it was a different animal.
pauses.reason: Scene turn from daylight description to night danger.

pauses.after: Callie stood twenty paces back in the dark and listened to it happen, and did not go up.
pauses.reason: Completed thought; transition to Callie's internal state.
Major emotional landing after the combat sequence ends abruptly.
Emphasis on the physical consequence of not removing the Edge.

pauses.after: She did it the way her grandfather had made her do it in a ditch when she was nine, with his hand on the back of her neck. Stop trying to see the thing. See the grade. She stopped looking at the grey part. She let her attention go along the steel the other way, backward, the way you walk a husk line backward to find out where it came from.
pauses.reason: Pause for Callie's internal realization process.
Isolating the key instruction for Callie's internal focus.
Revelation moment; allow the listener to register 'She was leaning'.
Critical realization; isolates the core mechanic of her power usage.

pauses.reason: Major emotional landing on Callie's physical and mental state after losing the Edge.

Reversal; isolates the new understanding of the Ward's direction.

pauses.after: Katori looked at her across the lamp for a long moment. Then she picked the lamp up and stood.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset; shift from internal realization to external action plan.
Completed thought in dialogue exchange regarding the strategy.

pauses.after: Ines cleaned it. Otto made a noise and then made himself stop making it.
pauses.reason: Pause after a physical action; transition to mother's command.

pauses.reason: Emotional landing on the contrast between Otto's pain and his attempt at humor.
